verdict.line: You lose the wave-trading phase through level 5 to Kled's E-Q burst, but win extended fights from level 11 onward once your Q stacks and his Skaarl bar runs out.

brief.thesis: Kled fights with two health bars: Skaarl absorbs damage until it hits zero, at which point Kled dismounts and deals less damage to champions. Nasus has almost no kill pressure before Q (Siphoning Strike, cooldown 8/7/6/5/4s, range 255) is stacked, so the entire lane is about surviving Kled's E (Jousting, cooldown 13/12/11/10/9s, range 550)-into-Q (Bear Trap on a Rope, cooldown 11/10/9/8/7s, range 800) burst until Skaarl's bar runs dry and your stacks catch up.

theirWindow.when: Skaarl's bar is full, Kled is mounted
theirWindow.what: He can Jousting dash in, immediately throw Bear Trap on a Rope to yank you, and follow with Violent Tendencies' four empowered attacks. Stay behind minions so his 800-range hook can't reach you without eating creep damage first.

yourWindow.when: Skaarl's bar is empty, Kled is dismounted
yourWindow.what: Dismounted Kled deals less damage to champions and his Q is replaced by Pocket Pistol, a knockback gun blast that pushes him away rather than hooking you in. Drop Spirit Fire (E) under him and commit with Q and Wither (W) while he's weak.

powerCurve.note: His E-Q threat live before your Q stacks

start.why: Measured in 79.8% of games and the stronger of the two starts (54% WR over 63 games) — the extra sustain against his E-dash autos and Q yank keeps you from getting zoned off farm before Q is stacked.

boots.why: Kled's entire early kit is auto-attack-reliant (Violent Tendencies' four empowered hits, Jousting autos on the dash-back), so flat armor from Steelcaps blunts more of his damage than Lucidity's cooldown refund does at this stage.

core.why: The most common first core item (70% over 10 games on this path) — gives you the stats to start winning trades instead of just surviving them.
Armor plus the attack speed slow directly answers Violent Tendencies' four-hit burst and Jousting autos.
Stacks with Soul Eater lifesteal to turn extended fights — the ones where Skaarl's bar runs out — into unwinnable sustain checks for Kled.

situational.when: his auto-attack damage through Skaarl is shredding you in trades
you want the wave-clear and slow utility over Trinity's raw stats
you are losing early all-ins and need cheap sustain to hold the lane

runes.keystoneWhy: The healing on movement plus the speed burst lets you step up for farm, soak chip damage from his autos, and reposition out of his 800-range Bear Trap on a Rope before it latches.

summoners.why: This is the single best-performing pair in the data (61.1% WR over 22.2% of games) — Flash lets you dodge the Jousting-into-hook combo or his all-in, and Teleport gets you back to lane fast enough to not lose plates while you're behind.

playing.title: Farm first, fight never before level 6
playing.detail: Siphoning Strike has no stacks yet and your trade range is 255 versus his 550-800 threat range. Take every safe last-hit and decline all-ins until Fury of the Sands (R) is live.

playing.title: Stay behind a minion buffer
playing.detail: Bear Trap on a Rope reaches 800 range and yanks you in — standing in front of your wave gives him a clean hook. Let creeps eat the first throw.

playing.title: Track the Skaarl bar before committing
playing.detail: A full Skaarl bar means the full E-Q-W burst is available; an empty one means Kled is weaker to champions and his Q is replaced by the ranged, non-hooking Pocket Pistol. Only all-in in the second state.

playing.title: Drop Spirit Fire before extended trades
playing.detail: Spirit Fire (E, cooldown 12s, range 650) reduces armor on anyone standing in it — place it under Kled before you commit so your Q and autos hit harder through the fight.

playing.title: Save Wither for his dash window
playing.detail: Wither (cooldown 15/14/13/12/11s, range 700) slows his movement and attack speed over time — hold it for when he's already committed Jousting and can't just walk away from the slow.

playing.title: Hold Fury of the Sands for 1v1s, not pokes
playing.detail: R is on a 120s cooldown and drains nearby enemies' max health into bonus damage over its duration, so it's built for a committed extended fight, not a quick trade — bait him into a long fight with your sustain first.

playing.title: Don't contest early skirmishes for kills
playing.detail: The data shows Kled holds the solo-kill advantage in this matchup, so look to out-scale through farm and Q stacks rather than force early duels you're not favored in.

brief.patchCaveat: The win rates, build path, runes, boots, and summoner spells above are measured from live games on the current patch (16.20.1) via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning — why the Skaarl bar matters, when to all-in, how to play around his dash-hook range — is this coach's own read of the ability data, not a measured stat.

stats.opponentTip: It is important to avoid Kled’s (E)-(Q) combo, keeping an eye out for his (Q) especially. Focus on farming with [Q] to gain stacks, while looking for an opportunity to nuke post-level 6 with Unsealed Spellbook + [R].
